problem: Embodied object-search tasks (ObjectNav, rearrangement) were mostly solved with RL plus hand-engineered exploration and coverage rewards, which are brittle, expensive to tune, and fail on longer-horizon tasks like pick-and-place. Existing human-demonstration datasets were too small to support imitation learning: EmbodiedQA has ~700 episodes, and CVDN, WAY and TEACh have under 10k. Shortest-path oracle demonstrations contain no exploration.
motivation: Object search needs sophisticated exploration: semantic priors, peeking into rooms, looking around, and exhaustive search. Humans do this naturally, but it is hard to express as a reward and absent from shortest-path demos. If human demos can be collected safely and cheaply at scale through browser-based teleoperation, large-scale IL becomes a realistic alternative to RL, and its data-scaling behaviour can be measured.
key_idea: Build a browser-based Habitat (WebGL) + Mechanical Turk virtual-teleoperation pipeline, collect ~92k human demonstrations (80k ObjectNav, 12k Pick&Place), and train a plain CNN+GRU policy by behavior cloning with inflection weighting. This outperforms reward-engineered RL.
insight: The exploration behaviour lives in the human data, not in the architecture. With roughly matched training steps (8.4M vs 7.6M), BC on 35k human demos reaches 31.6% SR on MP3D val versus 4.4% for BC on 114k shortest paths: shortest paths are 'inimitable' because they contain no search. Behaviour metrics (Table 4) show the IL agent reproduces human search patterns, clearly more than RL: occupancy coverage 21.4 vs 14.6, peeks 19.6 vs 9.7, panoramic turns 4.3 vs 0.0, exhaustive search 55.3 vs 49.0. Accuracy rises with dataset size from 4k to 70k without saturating. IL needs ~7x fewer unique environment steps than RL but not less wall-clock time. Adding 10k THDA demos (pure exhaustive search) helps by +0.8 SR. Swapping 10k MP3D demos for 10k Gibson demos hurts by 1.5 SR. Removing the predicted semantic inputs (SemSeg + goal-exists fraction) costs 8.9 SR.
method: Habitat-WebGL + AMT infrastructure: Habitat-Sim compiled to JavaScript/WebGL with Habitat 2.0 physics bindings, served via PsiTurk/NGINX/MySQL. Users teleoperate a LoCoBot by keyboard from its first-person RGB view (no depth or GPS). Actions are executed every 50 ms. Submissions are validated with the Habitat success checks (within 1 m for ObjectNav; object within 0.7 m of and above the receptacle centre for Pick&Place).

Datasets: ObjectNav-HD has 70k demos on 56 MP3D train scenes (~1250 per scene) plus 10k on 25 Gibson scenes, ~19.5M steps, avg 243 steps per episode; an extra 10k THDA-style demos (inserted objects) were also collected. PickPlace-HD has ~12k demos on 9 MP3D scenes over 457 object-receptacle pairs, ~11.5M steps, avg 932 steps. Step-matched shortest-path datasets were generated for comparison (114k ObjectNav, 25.7k Pick&Place).

Behavior cloning with inflection weighting: cross-entropy on human actions, with the loss at timesteps where a_t != a_{t-1} upweighted by (total actions / number of inflection points), following Wijmans et al. (EQA-MP3D).

ObjectNav policy: 640x480 RGB-D, avg-pooled; RGB goes through a randomly initialised ResNet18 and depth through a DD-PPO PointNav-pretrained ResNet50. Inputs also include a 32-d GPS+Compass embedding, a 32-d goal-category embedding, and semantic segmentation plus a 'Semantic Goal Exists' scalar from a frozen RedNet (SUN RGB-D pretrained, finetuned on 100k Habitat views), following Red Rabbit. Everything is concatenated into a 2-layer 512-d GRU, trained ~400M steps (~21 epochs on 70k demos).

Pick&Place policy: 256x256 RGB-D encoders as above plus a single-layer-LSTM embedding of the instruction 'Place the <object> on the <receptacle>', fed to a 2-layer 512-d GRU. Trained ~90M steps (~10 epochs on 9.5k demos) with the magic-pointer grab/release abstraction.

Behavior characterization metrics: Occupancy Coverage (2.5 m voxels), Sight Coverage, Goal Room Time Spent, Peeks, Panoramic Turns, Beeline, and Exhaustive Search (>=75% sight coverage). Computed from MP3D room bounding boxes to quantify search strategies of IL, RL and humans.

setting.backbone: CNN+GRU trained by behavior cloning: ResNet18 RGB encoder (from scratch) + ResNet50 depth encoder (DD-PPO PointNav-pretrained) + frozen RedNet semantic segmentation + 2-layer 512-d GRU; Pick&Place variant adds a single-layer LSTM instruction encoder
setting.training_data: ObjectNav: 70k human teleoperation demos on 56 MP3D train scenes (main model); variants use 35k / 50k (+10k THDA demos) / 80k (incl. 10k Gibson demos); ~19.5M steps for all 80k. Pick&Place: 9.5k human demos on 7 of 9 MP3D scenes (2 held out for New Envs), ~12k collected in total. RedNet finetuned on 100k Habitat-rendered views.
setting.observation: ObjectNav: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, avg-pooled) + GPS/compass + goal category + predicted semantic segmentation (RedNet); Pick&Place: egocentric RGB-D 256x256 + templated language instruction
setting.action_space: ObjectNav: discrete MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 30°, STOP (500-step limit, 1 m success). Pick&Place: MOVE_FORWARD/BACKWARD 0.15 m, TURN 5°, LOOK_UP/DOWN 5°, GRAB_RELEASE (magic pointer, 1.5 m), NO_OP, STOP (1500-step limit)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Habitat-Sim / Habitat 2.0 physics; MP3D and Gibson scenes; WebGL build for data collection)
setting.privileged: none (standard GPS+Compass sensor; semantics are predicted by RedNet, not ground truth)

numbers_note: Some results appear only in figures: the scaling curves (val success vs 4k–70k demos; Pick&Place 2.5k–9.5k), the sample-efficiency plots (IL vs RL success vs total and unique steps), and GRTS per scene. Three text/table inconsistencies: (1) the Gibson zero-shot text says a 40k-demo policy with 49.4% SR, while the table row says 70k demos with 49.5%; (2) the text cites 'row 11' for the 10k-Gibson+60k-MP3D variant (33.9/9.7), which is row 10 in the table; (3) the text says RL 'Red Rabbit' is row 3. Pick&Place RL got 0% success and is reported only in text. Other variants: 50k demos 32.4/9.1; 50k incl. 10k THDA 33.2/9.5; 70k incl. 10k Gibson 33.9/9.7; IL w/ shortest paths 4.4/2.2; human baseline 93.7/42.5 on MP3D val.
results: On MP3D ObjectNav val, BC on 70k human demos reaches 35.4% SR / 10.2% SPL, edging out Red Rabbit RL (34.6/7.9, trained on 240k agent trajectories, i.e. ~4 agent episodes per human demo). It clearly beats EmbCLIP (21.6/8.7) and ExploreTillSeen+THDA (28.4/11.0, which has higher SPL). On the Habitat Challenge test-std it gets 27.8/9.9, beating Red Rabbit 6-Act Base (24.5/6.4) and ExploreTillSeen+THDA (21.1/8.8). BC on shortest paths gets only 4.4/2.2. On Pick&Place, IL on 9.5k demos reaches 17.5% SR (test, new inits) and 8.3% in new environments, while shortest-path IL stays at ≤1.7% and reward-engineered RL at 0%. Transferred zero-shot to Gibson it gets 49.5/16.4, below SemExp (54.4/19.9) and PONI (73.6/41.0).
limitations: Plain behavior cloning (with inflection weighting) inherits covariate-shift issues. Common failures: stopping just outside the goal radius, pushing into collisions and getting stuck, looping among multiple goal instances until the step limit, and not finding the goal.

Relies on costly human data collection (~22.6k robot-hours equivalent). IL needs long training schedules, so wall-clock training is not cheaper than RL. SPL remains low (~10%), and even humans get only 42.5% SPL.

Simple CNN+RNN policy without mapping. It depends on RedNet semantic features (−8.9 SR without them). Pick&Place uses only 9 scenes and a magic-pointer grasp abstraction, so generalization to new environments is weak (8.3% SR).
